title: Motives, capabilities and choices together
statement: Explain a historical development as conditions, motives, capabilities and choices working together, keeping what made it desirable apart from what made it possible, never one cause alone.
detail: An AP history course's design document names two predictable misconceptions: a motive slogan for exploration that confuses goals with the capabilities that made voyages possible, and environmental determinism, in which geography automatically produces one social form. Its model has a valid explanation combine a motive, an institution that supplied resources and authority, a capability that solved a concrete problem, and information that changed later decisions, and it sets a multicausal boundary: neither a ship design nor an instrument began exploration by itself. The course's unit specifications warn in the same way against presenting a transformation as automatic and single-cause.
against: Both cited documents are marked "Historical / superseded" and record an earlier plan-review phase of the course (`grade3-reading/_archive/2026-08-13-consolidation/apush-corpus-hardening-20260731-tip.tar.gz::apush/docs/BRAINLIFT.md` and `grade3-reading/_archive/2026-08-13-consolidation/apush-corpus-hardening-20260731-tip.tar.gz::apush/docs/UNIT-SPECS.md`, line 5). The position is a design choice, not a measured result.

evidence.quote: Students frequently explain European exploration with a slogan such as God, gold, and glory. That list confuses goals with the capabilities that made sustained voyages possible.

A valid explanation shows combination: a motive made a voyage desirable; a state, commercial, or religious institution supplied resources and authority; a maritime capability addressed a concrete navigation or vessel problem; and information from voyages changed later decisions. The model also sets a multicausal boundary. A caravel or astrolabe did not initiate exploration by itself.

A second risk is environmental determinism: stating that geography automatically produced a single social form. The course teaches bounded regional cases and the interaction of constraint, opportunity, knowledge, technology, coordination, and choice.
do not present reform as one unified movement or the Market Revolution as an automatic, single-cause transformation.
